test_cases.description: NewRunner returns a non-nil *GitRunner with the specified workDir and no error, performing no validation of workDir existence at construction time.
preconditions: internal/gitcmd package is compiled
No git binary invocation occurs during construction
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner = NewRunner('/tmp/some/nonexistent/path', 'GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=Bot'); assert runner != nil

test_cases.description: Every exec.Cmd environment built by GitRunner concatenates os.Environ(), caller-supplied env, then safety defaults, with safety-default keys deduplicated from earlier entries.
preconditions: A GitRunner is constructed with NewRunner(workDir, 'GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=1')
os.Environ() may or may not contain safety-default keys
A real temporary git repo exists at workDir (created via git init)
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner = NewRunner(workDir, 'GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=1'); stdout, _, err = runner.Run(ctx, 'env'); assert err == nil; assert stdout contains 'GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0'; assert stdout contains 'GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file:https:ssh'; assert stdout contains 'GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1'; assert stdout does NOT contain 'GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=1' (only the safety default value appears)

test_cases.description: Every git subprocess receives GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL='file:https:ssh', GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT='0', and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM='1' as the final environment entries, hardcoded and not overridable.
preconditions: A GitRunner is constructed with NewRunner(workDir) with no extra env
A real temporary git repo exists at workDir
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner = NewRunner(workDir); stdout, _, err = runner.Run(ctx, 'env'); assert err == nil; assert stdout contains 'GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file:https:ssh'; assert stdout contains 'GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0'; assert stdout contains 'GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1'

test_cases.description: Multiple goroutines can call Run and RunExitCode concurrently on the same *GitRunner without data races.
preconditions: A GitRunner is constructed with NewRunner(workDir)
A real temporary git repo exists at workDir
Go race detector is enabled (go test -race)

expected.result: All goroutines complete without data race detected by -race flag

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner = NewRunner(workDir); wg = WaitGroup; for i in 0..9: wg.Add(1); go func() { runner.Run(ctx, 'version'); wg.Done() }(); wg.Wait(); // run with go test -race — no race condition reported

test_cases.description: Run returns stdout bytes, stderr bytes, and nil error when git exits with code 0.
preconditions: A GitRunner is constructed with NewRunner(workDir)
A real temporary git repo exists at workDir (git init already run)
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner = NewRunner(workDir); stdout, stderr, err = runner.Run(ctx, 'version'); assert err == nil; assert len(stdout) > 0; assert string(stdout) contains 'git version'

test_cases.description: Run returns a *GitError with Command (joined args without 'git' prefix), ExitCode, and Stderr fields when git exits non-zero, and Error() produces the exact format string.
preconditions: A GitRunner is constructed with NewRunner(workDir)
A real temporary git repo exists at workDir
No remote named 'origin' is configured (so 'git fetch nonexistent-remote' will fail)

expected.Error(): string matching 'git fetch nonexistent-remote-xyz exited with code <N>: <stderr>'

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner = NewRunner(workDir); _, _, err = runner.Run(ctx, 'fetch', 'nonexistent-remote-xyz'); assert err != nil; var gitErr *GitError; assert errors.As(err, &gitErr) == true; assert gitErr.Command == 'fetch nonexistent-remote-xyz'; assert gitErr.ExitCode != 0; assert len(gitErr.Stderr) > 0; assert gitErr.Error() == 'git fetch nonexistent-remote-xyz exited with code ' + str(gitErr.ExitCode) + ': ' + gitErr.Stderr

test_cases.description: Run returns the raw *exec.Error (not a *GitError) when the git binary is not found on PATH.
preconditions: A GitRunner is constructed but the PATH is manipulated so 'git' binary cannot be found
workDir is a valid directory
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner = NewRunner(workDir); // manipulate PATH so git is not found; _, _, err = runner.Run(ctx, 'version'); assert err != nil; var gitErr *GitError; assert errors.As(err, &gitErr) == false; var execErr *exec.Error; assert errors.As(err, &execErr) == true

test_cases.description: Run sends SIGKILL on context cancellation and returns partial stdout/stderr alongside the context error; both err != nil and len(stdout) > 0 may be true simultaneously.
preconditions: A GitRunner is constructed with NewRunner(workDir)
A real temporary git repo exists at workDir
A context with cancel function is created
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: ctx, cancel = context.WithCancel(context.Background()); runner = NewRunner(workDir); go func() { sleep(10ms); cancel() }(); stdout, stderr, err = runner.Run(ctx, 'log', '--all'); assert err != nil; // both err != nil and len(stdout) >= 0 are valid simultaneously — no assertion that stdout is empty

test_cases.description: RunExitCode returns stdout, stderr, the raw exit code, and nil error when the subprocess completes (including non-zero exit), making the exit code meaningful.
preconditions: A GitRunner is constructed with NewRunner(workDir)
A real temporary git repo exists at workDir

expected.exitCode: non-zero integer (2 or 128 depending on git behavior)

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner = NewRunner(workDir); stdout, stderr, exitCode, err = runner.RunExitCode(ctx, 'ls-remote', '--exit-code', 'file:///nonexistent-path-xyz', 'refs/heads/main'); assert err == nil; assert exitCode != 0; // exitCode is meaningful

test_cases.description: RunExitCode returns err != nil wrapped via fmt.Errorf('%w', ...) for system-level failures, preserving the underlying os/exec error for errors.Is/errors.As, and never produces a GitError.
preconditions: A GitRunner is constructed but PATH is manipulated so 'git' binary cannot be found
workDir is a valid directory
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner = NewRunner(workDir); // manipulate PATH; _, _, exitCode, err = runner.RunExitCode(ctx, 'version'); assert err != nil; var gitErr *GitError; assert errors.As(err, &gitErr) == false; var execErr *exec.Error; assert errors.As(err, &execErr) == true

test_cases.description: RunExitCode returns err != nil and exitCode == -1 when context cancellation causes SIGKILL signal termination.
preconditions: A GitRunner is constructed with NewRunner(workDir)
A real temporary git repo exists at workDir
A context with cancel function is created
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: ctx, cancel = context.WithCancel(context.Background()); runner = NewRunner(workDir); go func() { sleep(10ms); cancel() }(); _, _, exitCode, err = runner.RunExitCode(ctx, 'log', '--all'); assert err != nil; assert exitCode == -1

test_cases.description: RunExitCode never produces a *GitError under any circumstances, including non-zero exit codes.
preconditions: A GitRunner is constructed with NewRunner(workDir)
A real temporary git repo exists at workDir

expected.GitError: NOT produced — errors.As(err, &*GitError{}) returns false for any error returned by RunExitCode
expected.err: nil (non-zero exit is not a system error)

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner = NewRunner(workDir); _, _, exitCode, err = runner.RunExitCode(ctx, 'fetch', 'nonexistent-remote-xyz'); assert err == nil; assert exitCode != 0; var gitErr *GitError; assert errors.As(err, &gitErr) == false

property_tests.description: For any GitRunner constructed with any workDir and any env strings (including safety-default keys with arbitrary values), every subprocess always receives the three safety defaults as the final environment entries.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample 50 combinations: workDir from {valid temp dir, empty string, '/nonexistent'}; env from {empty, ['GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=ext::'], ['GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=1', 'GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=0'], all three safety keys with wrong values, unrelated keys}
property_tests.invariant_check: For each combination: runner = NewRunner(workDir, ...env); stdout, _, err = runner.Run(ctx, 'env'); if err == nil: assert stdout contains 'GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file:https:ssh'; assert stdout contains 'GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0'; assert stdout contains 'GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1'; assert count('GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=', stdout) == 1; assert count('GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=', stdout) == 1; assert count('GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=', stdout) == 1

property_tests.description: For any call to GitRunner.Run with any args, Run returns a non-nil *GitError if and only if git exits non-zero, and never returns a *GitError for system-level failures.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample 30 arg combinations: {['version'] (exit 0), ['fetch', 'nonexistent-remote'] (exit non-zero), [] (exit non-zero), ['--invalid-flag'] (exit non-zero)}; also test with PATH cleared (binary not found) and cancelled context
property_tests.invariant_check: For each case: _, _, err = runner.Run(ctx, ...args); var gitErr *GitError; isGitErr = errors.As(err, &gitErr); if subprocess exited non-zero: assert isGitErr == true; if subprocess exited 0: assert err == nil; if binary not found or context cancelled: assert isGitErr == false

property_tests.description: For any call to GitRunner.RunExitCode with any args and any context state, RunExitCode never returns a *GitError.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample 30 combinations: args from {['version'], ['fetch', 'nonexistent-remote'], [], ['--invalid-flag']}; context from {valid, pre-cancelled, 1ms deadline}; PATH from {valid, cleared}
property_tests.invariant_check: For each combination: _, _, _, err = runner.RunExitCode(ctx, ...args); var gitErr *GitError; assert errors.As(err, &gitErr) == false // always, regardless of outcome

property_tests.description: For any call to GitRunner.BranchExists, (false, nil) is returned if and only if git ls-remote exits with code 2; any other non-zero exit returns (false, error); exit 0 returns (true, nil).
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample using a local bare repo: {branch that exists (exit 0), branch that does not exist (exit 2), invalid remote path (exit 128), pre-cancelled context (system error)}
property_tests.invariant_check: exists, err = runner.BranchExists(ctx, remote, branch); if exitCode == 0: assert exists == true AND err == nil; if exitCode == 2: assert exists == false AND err == nil; if exitCode is non-zero and non-2: assert exists == false AND err != nil; if system error: assert exists == false AND err != nil

property_tests.description: For any *GitError with any Command, ExitCode, and Stderr values, Error() always returns a string matching the exact pattern 'git <Command> exited with code <ExitCode>: <Stderr>'.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample 50 GitError values: Command from {'rebase origin/main', 'fetch', '', 'merge-tree --write-tree HEAD~1 HEAD'}; ExitCode from {1, 2, 128, -1, 0}; Stderr from {'', 'error: conflict', 'fatal: repository not found', string of 1000 chars}
property_tests.invariant_check: gitErr = &GitError{Command: cmd, ExitCode: code, Stderr: stderr}; result = gitErr.Error(); assert result == 'git ' + cmd + ' exited with code ' + str(code) + ': ' + stderr

property_tests.description: For any installed git version below 2.38, CheckGitVersion returns an error whose message exactly matches 'requires git >= 2.38, found <installed>'.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample 10 below-minimum version strings via fake git binaries: {'git version 2.37.9', 'git version 2.0.0', 'git version 1.9.5', 'git version 2.37.0', 'git version 2.36.3'}
property_tests.invariant_check: err = CheckGitVersion(ctx); assert err != nil; assert err.Error() == 'requires git >= 2.38, found ' + parsedVersion // where parsedVersion is the first three numeric components

property_tests.description: For any bare branch name passed to BranchExists, the git ls-remote command always receives 'refs/heads/<branch>' as the ref argument, never the bare branch name directly.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample 20 branch names: {'main', 'feature/foo', 'release-1.0', 'a', 'very/deeply/nested/branch', 'branch-with-dashes'}; use a bare repo and verify the correct ref is queried
property_tests.invariant_check: For each branch name: bareRepo = createBareRepo(); pushBranch(bareRepo, branch); exists, err = runner.BranchExists(ctx, bareRepo, branch); assert exists == true AND err == nil; // Also verify that querying 'refs/heads/' + branch directly via RunExitCode returns the same result

property_tests.description: Any number of goroutines calling Run or RunExitCode concurrently on the same *GitRunner produce no data races, verified by the Go race detector.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Run with goroutine counts from {2, 5, 10, 20}; args from {['version'], ['--version']}; use go test -race flag
property_tests.invariant_check: runner = NewRunner(workDir); wg = WaitGroup; for i in 0..N: wg.Add(1); go func() { runner.Run(ctx, 'version'); wg.Done() }(); wg.Wait(); // go test -race reports no data race

property_tests.description: For any git --version output string on supported platforms, CheckGitVersion extracts exactly the first three dot-separated numeric components and ignores all trailing tokens.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample 20 version strings: standard ('git version 2.39.1'), Apple Git ('git version 2.39.3 (Apple Git-145)'), RC ('git version 2.38.0.rc1'), with extra tokens ('git version 2.40.0 extra token'), with build metadata ('git version 2.39.0+dfsg-1')
property_tests.invariant_check: For each versionStr: parsed = parseVersionComponents(versionStr); assert len(parsed) == 3; assert all components are non-negative integers; assert no trailing tokens are included in the comparison; // Verify by checking that 'git version 2.39.3 (Apple Git-145)' parses to [2, 39, 3] not [2, 39] or [2, 39, 3, 145]
